```{r setup, include = FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(echo = TRUE, message = FALSE, warning = FALSE,
                      fig.align = "center", comment = "#>")
options(width = 110, scipen = 0)
```

This file reproduces every number, table and figure in our Part 1 proposal.
It uses only base R plus the `car` package (for Levene's test).
Place it in the project folder next to `data/` and `figures/` and knit; all paths are relative.

**Research question.** Among newly built, detached single-family homes sold in the United States in 2025,
how much does additional finished floor area add to the sale price, and does this marginal price of floor
area differ across the nine Census divisions, after accounting for lot size, room counts, garage,
foundation, exterior wall material, heating fuel and the other structural features listed below?

```{r packages}
library(car)      # leveneTest() only
set.seed(302)     # no random numbers are drawn below; the train/test split is read from a file (Section 5)
dir.create("figures", showWarnings = FALSE)
dir.create("data/cleaned", showWarnings = FALSE, recursive = TRUE)
```

# Read the original data

The original file is the 2025 annual microdata file of the U.S. Census Bureau's Survey of Construction (SOC),
downloaded from <https://www.census.gov/construction/chars/microdata.html> (`soc25.xlsx`, saved as CSV
without any other change). Variable definitions are in `data/original/socmicro_info.pdf`.

```{r read-raw}
raw <- read.csv("data/original/soc25.csv")
dim(raw)
```

# Cleaning: one filter at a time

Each step below prints the number of rows that remain. The codes used come from `socmicro_info.pdf`
(for example, `0` or `9` means "not reported" for the categorical fields).

```{r clean-function}
clean_soc <- function(raw, year) {
  steps <- data.frame(step = character(0), rows_remaining = integer(0))
  add <- function(label, d) {
    steps[nrow(steps) + 1, ] <<- list(label, nrow(d))
    d
  }
  s <- add(sprintf("All %d SOC records", year), raw)
  s <- add("CAT = 1 (house built for sale)", s[s$CAT == 1, ])
  s <- add(sprintf("Sales contract signed in %d", year),
           s[s$SALE >= year * 100 + 1 & s$SALE <= year * 100 + 12, ])
  s <- add("Sale price reported (SLPR > 0)", s[s$SLPR > 0, ])
  s <- add("Detached (DET = 1) and not in a condominium project (CON = 2)",
           s[s$DET == 1 & s$CON == 2, ])
  s <- add("Floor area and lot size reported (SQFS > 0, AREA > 0)",
           s[s$SQFS > 0 & s$AREA > 0, ])
  # valid (reported) codes of the 12 categorical source fields
  valid <- list(STOR = 1:3, BEDR = 2:5, FULB = 1:4, HAFB = 0:2, GAR = 1:4, BASE = 1:4,
                FPLS = 0:2, ASSOC = 1:2, AGER = 1:2, WAL1 = c(1, 2, 4:9), FUEL = 1:5,
                SEWER = 1:3)
  ok <- rep(TRUE, nrow(s))
  for (v in names(valid)) ok <- ok & s[[v]] %in% valid[[v]]
  s <- add("No 'not reported' code in any categorical predictor", s[ok, ])
  list(data = s, steps = steps)
}

cl <- clean_soc(raw, 2025)
cl$steps
stopifnot(nrow(cl$data) == 6185)
```

# Construct the analysis variables

* `price_k`: sale price in $1,000s (SLPR / 1000; the price includes the improved lot).
* `sqft100`: finished floor area in 100s of square feet (SQFS / 100).
* `lot_k`: lot size in 1,000s of square feet (AREA / 1000).
* `sale_month`: month the sales contract was signed (1--12).
* `stage`: construction stage when the contract was signed, derived from the sale, start and completion
  dates only (never from the price).
* Categorical predictors are recoded to readable labels; the first level listed is the reference level.
  WAL1 "concrete block" (code 6) is grouped with "other" (code 9); FUEL "oil" (4) is grouped with
  "other/no heat" (5); SEWER "other" (3, six houses) is grouped with individual septic systems (2).
* `slpr_flag` (price top/bottom-coded by the Census Bureau) and `weight` (sampling weight) are kept for
  later sensitivity checks; they are **not** predictors.

```{r construct-function}
recode <- function(x, map) unname(map[as.character(x)])
ym <- function(x) (x %/% 100) * 12 + x %% 100            # YYYYMM -> month count

division_levels <- c("SouthAtlantic", "NewEngland", "MidAtlantic", "ENCentral", "WNCentral",
                     "ESCentral", "WSCentral", "Mountain", "Pacific")
factor_levels <- list(
  division = division_levels,
  stories = c("1", "2", "3plus"),
  bedrooms = c("2orless", "3", "4", "5plus"),
  fullbath = c("1orless", "2", "3", "4plus"),
  halfbath = c("0", "1", "2plus"),
  garage = c("1car", "2car", "3plus", "other"),
  foundation = c("basement", "crawl", "slab", "other"),
  fireplace = c("0", "1", "2plus"),
  hoa = c("no", "yes"),
  age_restricted = c("no", "yes"),
  wall = c("brick", "wood", "stucco", "vinyl", "stone", "fibercement", "other"),
  heat_fuel = c("electric", "gas", "propane", "other"),
  sewer = c("public", "septic"),
  stage = c("completed", "under_constr", "not_started"))

construct_soc <- function(s) {
  sale_m <- ym(s$SALE)
  strt_m <- ifelse(s$STRT > 0, ym(s$STRT), 1e9)
  comp_m <- ifelse(s$COMP > 0, ym(s$COMP), 1e9)
  data.frame(
    id = s$ID,
    price_k = s$SLPR / 1000,
    sqft100 = s$SQFS / 100,
    lot_k = s$AREA / 1000,
    division = recode(s$DIV, c("1" = "NewEngland", "2" = "MidAtlantic", "3" = "ENCentral",
                               "4" = "WNCentral", "5" = "SouthAtlantic", "6" = "ESCentral",
                               "7" = "WSCentral", "8" = "Mountain", "9" = "Pacific")),
    stories = recode(s$STOR, c("1" = "1", "2" = "2", "3" = "3plus")),
    bedrooms = recode(s$BEDR, c("2" = "2orless", "3" = "3", "4" = "4", "5" = "5plus")),
    fullbath = recode(s$FULB, c("1" = "1orless", "2" = "2", "3" = "3", "4" = "4plus")),
    halfbath = recode(s$HAFB, c("0" = "0", "1" = "1", "2" = "2plus")),
    garage = recode(s$GAR, c("1" = "1car", "2" = "2car", "3" = "3plus", "4" = "other")),
    foundation = recode(s$BASE, c("1" = "basement", "2" = "crawl", "3" = "slab", "4" = "other")),
    fireplace = recode(s$FPLS, c("0" = "0", "1" = "1", "2" = "2plus")),
    hoa = recode(s$ASSOC, c("1" = "yes", "2" = "no")),
    age_restricted = recode(s$AGER, c("1" = "yes", "2" = "no")),
    wall = recode(s$WAL1, c("1" = "wood", "2" = "brick", "4" = "stucco", "5" = "vinyl",
                            "6" = "other", "7" = "stone", "8" = "fibercement", "9" = "other")),
    heat_fuel = recode(s$FUEL, c("1" = "electric", "2" = "gas", "3" = "propane",
                                 "4" = "other", "5" = "other")),
    sewer = recode(s$SEWER, c("1" = "public", "2" = "septic", "3" = "septic")),
    sale_month = s$SALE %% 100,
    stage = ifelse(sale_m < strt_m, "not_started",
                   ifelse(sale_m < comp_m, "under_constr", "completed")),
    slpr_flag = s$SLPR_F,
    weight = s$WEIGHT,
    stringsAsFactors = FALSE)
}

as_model_factors <- function(d) {
  for (v in names(factor_levels)) d[[v]] <- factor(d[[v]], levels = factor_levels[[v]])
  d
}

soc <- construct_soc(cl$data)
stopifnot(!anyNA(soc), !anyDuplicated(soc$id))
dim(soc)
```

# Attach the archived train/test split and write the cleaned file

The 70/30 train/test split was fixed **once, at the start of the project, and archived** in
`data/split_ids.csv` (columns `id`, `split`). It was produced in Python with
`numpy.random.default_rng(302).permutation(6185)` applied to the rows of the cleaned data in the order
above, with the first 4,330 permuted rows forming the training set. We read the archived file instead of
re-drawing the split in R (`set.seed(302)` in R would give a different split). This guarantees that the
test set is the same one that was set aside before any modelling and that it has never been looked at:
every table, figure and model in this file uses the training rows only.

```{r split-and-write}
split_ids <- read.csv("data/split_ids.csv")
stopifnot(nrow(split_ids) == nrow(soc), setequal(split_ids$id, soc$id))
soc$split <- split_ids$split[match(soc$id, split_ids$id)]
table(soc$split)

write.csv(soc, "data/cleaned/soc_clean.csv", row.names = FALSE)
```

# Keep the training set only

```{r train}
train <- as_model_factors(soc[soc$split == "train", ])
nrow(train)
```

# Variable summary (training set, n = 4,330)

Skewness is the moment coefficient $g_1 = m_3 / m_2^{3/2}$. After cleaning no variable has missing values
(rows with "not reported" codes were removed in Section 2).

```{r summary-table}
skew <- function(x) { z <- x - mean(x); mean(z^3) / mean(z^2)^1.5 }
exkurt <- function(x) { z <- x - mean(x); mean(z^4) / mean(z^2)^2 - 3 }

num_vars <- c(price_k = "Response: sale price ($1000s)",
              sqft100 = "Finished floor area (100 sq ft)",
              lot_k = "Lot size (1000 sq ft)",
              sale_month = "Month contract signed (1-12)")
num_tab <- data.frame(
  variable = names(num_vars), description = unname(num_vars),
  mean = sapply(names(num_vars), function(v) mean(train[[v]])),
  sd = sapply(names(num_vars), function(v) sd(train[[v]])),
  min = sapply(names(num_vars), function(v) min(train[[v]])),
  median = sapply(names(num_vars), function(v) median(train[[v]])),
  max = sapply(names(num_vars), function(v) max(train[[v]])),
  skewness = sapply(names(num_vars), function(v) skew(train[[v]])),
  missing = sapply(names(num_vars), function(v) sum(is.na(train[[v]]))),
  row.names = NULL)
knitr::kable(num_tab, digits = 2, caption = "Numerical variables (training set)")

cat_vars <- names(factor_levels)
cat_tab <- data.frame(
  variable = cat_vars,
  levels = sapply(cat_vars, function(v) nlevels(train[[v]])),
  counts = sapply(cat_vars, function(v) {
    tb <- table(train[[v]]); paste(names(tb), tb, sep = ": ", collapse = "; ")
  }),
  missing = sapply(cat_vars, function(v) sum(is.na(train[[v]]))),
  row.names = NULL)
knitr::kable(cat_tab, caption = "Categorical variables (training set; first level = reference)")
```

# Why an interaction between floor area and division?

Hedonic price theory (Rosen, 1974) treats the slope of price on a characteristic as that characteristic's
implicit price, which is set in each market separately; construction costs (Gyourko & Saiz, 2006) and
regulation (Glaeser, Gyourko & Saks, 2005) differ across U.S. regions. The figure below shows that the
simple (unadjusted) slope of price on floor area differs clearly across divisions in the training data.

```{r interaction-plot, fig.width = 10, fig.height = 4.4}
within_slopes <- t(sapply(division_levels, function(g) {
  fit <- lm(price_k ~ sqft100, data = train[train$division == g, ])
  ci <- confint(fit)["sqft100", ]
  c(n = sum(train$division == g), slope = unname(coef(fit)["sqft100"]),
    lower = unname(ci[1]), upper = unname(ci[2]))
}))
round(within_slopes, 2)

draw_interaction <- function() {
  layout(matrix(1:2, 1), widths = c(1, 1.1))
  par(mar = c(4.5, 5, 3, 1), las = 1)
  plot(train$sqft100 * 100, train$price_k, pch = 16, cex = 0.35, col = "grey80",
       xlab = "Finished floor area (sq ft)", ylab = "Sale price ($1000s)",
       main = "(a) Price vs floor area, one OLS line per division", cex.main = 1)
  for (g in division_levels) {
    dg <- train[train$division == g, ]
    fit <- lm(price_k ~ sqft100, data = dg)
    xs <- quantile(dg$sqft100, c(0.05, 0.95))
    lines(xs * 100, coef(fit)[1] + coef(fit)[2] * xs, col = div_col[g], lty = div_lty[g], lwd = 2.2)
  }
  legend("topleft", legend = div_lab[division_levels], col = div_col, lty = div_lty, lwd = 2,
         cex = 0.7, bg = "white", ncol = 2)
  o <- order(within_slopes[, "slope"])
  k <- length(o)
  par(mar = c(4.5, 10.5, 3, 1))
  plot(within_slopes[o, "slope"], seq_len(k), xlim = range(within_slopes[, c("lower", "upper")]),
       pch = 19, col = div_col[rownames(within_slopes)[o]], yaxt = "n", ylab = "",
       xlab = "$1000s per extra 100 sq ft",
       main = "(b) Within-division slopes with 95% CIs", cex.main = 1)
  segments(within_slopes[o, "lower"], seq_len(k), within_slopes[o, "upper"], seq_len(k),
           col = div_col[rownames(within_slopes)[o]], lwd = 2)
  axis(2, at = seq_len(k), labels = sprintf("%s (n=%d)", div_lab[rownames(within_slopes)[o]],
                                            within_slopes[o, "n"]), las = 1, cex.axis = 0.75)
  abline(v = mean(within_slopes[, "slope"]), lty = 3, col = "grey40")
}
fig_out("fig1_interaction.png", 10, 4.4, draw_interaction)
```

# Preliminary model (Part 1): raw sale price, 17 predictors

Seventeen predictors: 3 numerical (`sqft100`, `lot_k`, `sale_month`) and 14 categorical
(`division` and 13 structural/market features), plus the `sqft100 x division` interaction; 52 coefficients.
**No transformation or other correction is applied in Part 1.**

```{r model}
f1 <- price_k ~ sqft100 * division + lot_k + stories + bedrooms + fullbath + halfbath + garage +
  foundation + fireplace + hoa + age_restricted + wall + heat_fuel + sewer + stage + sale_month
m1 <- lm(f1, data = train)
s1 <- summary(m1)
c(n = nobs(m1), coefficients = length(coef(m1)), R2 = s1$r.squared, adj_R2 = s1$adj.r.squared,
  sigma = s1$sigma, F = unname(s1$fstatistic[1]), df1 = unname(s1$fstatistic[2]),
  df2 = unname(s1$fstatistic[3]))

# does the interaction matter? (nested F tests)
m1_noint <- update(m1, . ~ . - sqft100:division)
m1_noX   <- update(m1, . ~ . - sqft100:division - sqft100)
anova(m1_noint, m1)          # partial F for the 8 interaction coefficients
anova(m1_noX, m1)            # partial F for floor area and its interaction (9 coefficients)
c(dR2_interaction = s1$r.squared - summary(m1_noint)$r.squared,
  dR2_area_and_interaction = s1$r.squared - summary(m1_noX)$r.squared)
```

## Coefficient table with standard errors and 95% confidence intervals

```{r coef-table}
ci1 <- confint(m1)
coef_tab <- data.frame(term = names(coef(m1)), estimate = coef(m1),
                       se = s1$coefficients[, "Std. Error"], lower95 = ci1[, 1], upper95 = ci1[, 2],
                       t = s1$coefficients[, "t value"], p = s1$coefficients[, "Pr(>|t|)"],
                       row.names = NULL)
knitr::kable(coef_tab, digits = c(0, 3, 3, 3, 3, 2, 4),
             caption = "All 52 coefficients of the preliminary model (price in $1000s)")
```

## Slope of price on floor area in each division

Each division's slope is $\hat\beta_{\text{sqft100}} + \hat\beta_{\text{sqft100:division}_g}$
(the reference division, South Atlantic, has no interaction term). Its standard error comes from
$\mathbf{L}^\top \widehat{\operatorname{Var}}(\hat{\boldsymbol\beta}) \mathbf{L}$.

```{r division-slopes}
V1 <- vcov(m1)
slope_tab <- t(sapply(division_levels, function(g) {
  L <- setNames(numeric(length(coef(m1))), names(coef(m1)))
  L["sqft100"] <- 1
  if (g != "SouthAtlantic") L[paste0("sqft100:division", g)] <- 1
  est <- sum(L * coef(m1)); se <- sqrt(drop(t(L) %*% V1 %*% L))
  tq <- qt(0.975, df.residual(m1))
  c(n = sum(train$division == g), slope = est, se = se, lower95 = est - tq * se,
    upper95 = est + tq * se, p = 2 * pt(-abs(est / se), df.residual(m1)))
}))
knitr::kable(slope_tab, digits = c(0, 2, 2, 2, 2, 4),
             caption = "Adjusted slope of sale price ($1000s) per extra 100 sq ft, by division")
```

# Residual analysis of the preliminary model (no corrections)

```{r residual-quantities}
e1 <- resid(m1); yhat1 <- fitted(m1); r1 <- rstandard(m1)
num_preds <- c("sqft100", "lot_k", "sale_month")
# readable labels for the figures (the proposal shows these plots)
num_lab <- c(sqft100 = "Floor area (100 sq ft)", lot_k = "Lot size (1000 sq ft)",
             sale_month = "Month of sale")
num_short <- c(sqft100 = "floor area", lot_k = "lot size", sale_month = "month of sale")
cat_lab <- c(division = "Census division", stories = "Stories", bedrooms = "Bedrooms",
             fullbath = "Full bathrooms", halfbath = "Half bathrooms", garage = "Garage",
             foundation = "Foundation", fireplace = "Fireplaces", hoa = "Homeowners' association",
             age_restricted = "Age-restricted community", wall = "Exterior wall", heat_fuel = "Heating fuel",
             sewer = "Sewer", stage = "Construction stage at sale")
level_lab <- function(v) {
  l <- levels(train[[v]])
  if (v == "division") return(c("S Atlantic", "New England", "Mid Atlantic", "E N Central", "W N Central",
                                "E S Central", "W S Central", "Mountain", "Pacific"))
  map <- c("2orless" = "2 or fewer", "1orless" = "1 or fewer", "3plus" = "3+", "4plus" = "4+", "5plus" = "5+",
           "2plus" = "2+", "1car" = "1-car", "2car" = "2-car", "fibercement" = "fiber cement",
           "under_constr" = "under constr.", "not_started" = "not started", "septic" = "septic/other",
           "crawl" = "crawl space")
  if (v == "garage") map["3plus"] <- "3+-car"
  ifelse(l %in% names(map), map[l], l)
}
cat_preds <- names(factor_levels)
```

## Condition 1 (Y vs fitted) and Condition 2 (pairs of numerical predictors)

```{r conditions, fig.width = 8, fig.height = 6.6}
draw_conditions <- function() {
  par(mfrow = c(2, 2), mar = c(4.5, 5, 3, 1), las = 1)
  plot(yhat1, train$price_k, pch = 16, cex = 0.4, col = pt_col,
       xlab = "Fitted sale price ($1000s)", ylab = "Observed sale price ($1000s)",
       main = "Condition 1: Y vs fitted values", cex.main = 1)
  abline(0, 1, lty = 2)
  lines(lowess(yhat1, train$price_k, f = 0.3), col = ln_col, lwd = 2)
  prs <- combn(num_preds, 2)
  for (j in seq_len(ncol(prs))) {
    a <- prs[1, j]; b <- prs[2, j]
    xa <- train[[a]]; xb <- train[[b]]
    if (b == "sale_month") xb <- jitter(xb, amount = 0.25)
    plot(xa, xb, pch = 16, cex = 0.4, col = pt_col, xlab = num_lab[a], ylab = num_lab[b],
         main = sprintf("Condition 2: %s vs %s (r = %.2f)", num_short[b], num_short[a],
                        cor(train[[a]], train[[b]])),
         cex.main = 1)
    lines(lowess(train[[a]], train[[b]], f = 0.3), col = ln_col, lwd = 2)
  }
}
set.seed(302)  # for the jitter of sale_month in the plot only
fig_out("fig2_conditions.png", 8, 6.6, draw_conditions)
cor(train[, num_preds])
```

## Residuals vs fitted values, scale-location, normal QQ, and residuals vs each numerical predictor

```{r residual-grid, fig.width = 10, fig.height = 6.6}
draw_residuals <- function() {
  par(mfrow = c(2, 3), mar = c(4.5, 5, 3, 1), las = 1)
  plot(yhat1, e1, pch = 16, cex = 0.4, col = pt_col, xlab = "Fitted value ($1000s)",
       ylab = "Residual ($1000s)", main = "Residuals vs fitted", cex.main = 1)
  abline(h = 0, lty = 2); lines(lowess(yhat1, e1, f = 0.3), col = ln_col, lwd = 2)
  plot(yhat1, sqrt(abs(r1)), pch = 16, cex = 0.4, col = pt_col, xlab = "Fitted value ($1000s)",
       ylab = "sqrt(|standardized residual|)", main = "Scale-location", cex.main = 1)
  lines(lowess(yhat1, sqrt(abs(r1)), f = 0.3), col = ln_col, lwd = 2)
  qqnorm(r1, pch = 16, cex = 0.4, col = pt_col, main = "Normal QQ plot of standardized residuals",
         cex.main = 1)
  qqline(r1, col = ln_col, lwd = 2)
  for (v in num_preds) {
    plot(train[[v]], e1, pch = 16, cex = 0.4, col = pt_col, xlab = num_lab[v], ylab = "Residual ($1000s)",
         main = paste("Residuals vs", num_short[v]), cex.main = 1)
    abline(h = 0, lty = 2); lines(lowess(train[[v]], e1, f = 0.3), col = ln_col, lwd = 2)
  }
}
fig_out("fig3_residuals.png", 10, 6.6, draw_residuals)
```

## Residuals by each categorical predictor

Boxes show the residual distribution in each level (whiskers at 1.5 IQR; individual outlying points are
not drawn to keep the boxes readable -- see the QQ plot for the tails). The title gives the ratio of the
largest to the smallest residual SD across levels.

```{r residual-boxplots, fig.width = 10, fig.height = 13}
sd_ratio <- sapply(cat_preds, function(v) {
  s <- tapply(e1, train[[v]], sd); max(s) / min(s)
})
draw_boxplots <- function() {
  par(mfrow = c(5, 3), mar = c(7, 5, 3, 1))
  for (v in cat_preds) {
    boxplot(e1 ~ train[[v]], names = level_lab(v), outline = FALSE, las = 2, cex.axis = 0.85, xlab = "",
            ylab = "", col = "grey90",
            main = sprintf("%s (SD ratio %.1f)", cat_lab[v], sd_ratio[v]), cex.main = 1)
    abline(h = 0, col = ln_col, lty = 2)
    mtext("Residual ($1000s)", side = 2, line = 3.6, cex = 0.7)
  }
  hist(r1, breaks = 80, col = "grey80", border = "white", xlab = "Standardized residual",
       main = "Histogram of standardized residuals", cex.main = 1)
}
fig_out("fig4_resid_by_categorical.png", 10, 13, draw_boxplots)
```

## Numerical evidence for the assumption checks

```{r assumption-numbers}
# Breusch-Pagan (Koenker, studentized) statistic computed by hand: n * R^2 of e^2 on the design matrix
bp_koenker <- function(m) {
  e2 <- resid(m)^2; X <- model.matrix(m)
  aux <- lm.fit(X, e2)
  r2 <- 1 - sum(aux$residuals^2) / sum((e2 - mean(e2))^2)
  LM <- length(e2) * r2; df <- ncol(X) - 1
  c(LM = LM, df = df, p = pchisq(LM, df, lower.tail = FALSE))
}
bp1 <- bp_koenker(m1)
lev_div <- leveneTest(y = e1, group = train$division)          # Brown-Forsythe (median-centred) version
checks <- c(cor_Y_fitted = cor(train$price_k, yhat1),
            max_abs_cor_numeric_predictors = max(abs(cor(train[, num_preds])[upper.tri(diag(3))])),
            resid_skewness = skew(e1), resid_excess_kurtosis = exkurt(e1),
            BP_LM = unname(bp1["LM"]), BP_df = unname(bp1["df"]), BP_p = unname(bp1["p"]),
            levene_division_F = lev_div[1, "F value"], levene_division_p = lev_div[1, "Pr(>F)"],
            max_sd_ratio_division = unname(sd_ratio["division"]),
            n_abs_std_resid_gt_4 = sum(abs(r1) > 4), max_abs_std_resid = max(abs(r1)))
round(checks, 4)
round(sd_ratio, 2)
# errors across time: mean residual by sale month (a trend would suggest time dependence)
round(tapply(e1, train$sale_month, mean), 1)
```

## Conclusions for each assumption (no corrections made in Part 1)

* **Condition 1 (Y vs fitted): approximately holds.** The observed prices scatter around a single
  increasing curve close to the identity line (correlation `r sprintf("%.2f", checks["cor_Y_fitted"])`),
  but the spread widens sharply at high fitted values. Because both conditions hold reasonably, the
  residual plots can be used to diagnose which assumption fails.
* **Condition 2 (numerical predictors vs each other): holds.** The pairwise plots show no curved
  patterns; the largest absolute correlation among `sqft100`, `lot_k` and `sale_month` is
  `r sprintf("%.2f", checks["max_abs_cor_numeric_predictors"])`.
* **Linearity: mildly violated.** The LOWESS curve of residuals vs fitted values is slightly U-shaped, and
  residuals vs `sqft100` bend away from zero at the largest floor areas. `lot_k` and `sale_month` show no
  systematic pattern.
* **Constant variance: clearly violated.** Residuals vs fitted values fan out (funnel shape) and the
  scale-location curve rises steadily. The Breusch-Pagan (Koenker) statistic is
  `r sprintf("%.0f", checks["BP_LM"])` on `r checks["BP_df"]` df; residual SDs differ across divisions by a
  factor of `r sprintf("%.1f", checks["max_sd_ratio_division"])` (Levene p =
  `r format(checks["levene_division_p"], digits = 2)`), and also across stories, bathrooms and other levels.
* **Normality: clearly violated.** The QQ plot has a long, steep upper tail; residual skewness is
  `r sprintf("%.2f", checks["resid_skewness"])` and excess kurtosis
  `r sprintf("%.1f", checks["resid_excess_kurtosis"])`, with `r checks["n_abs_std_resid_gt_4"]`
  standardized residuals beyond +/-4. Part of the tail is caused by the Census top-coding of prices.
* **Uncorrelated errors: plausible by design, cannot be fully tested.** SOC is a probability sample of
  building permits, each row is a different house, and all rows are one cross-section (2025 contracts);
  the order of houses in the file is randomly scrambled within division, so a residual-vs-order plot
  carries no information. Residuals show no trend across sale months. The public file has no subdivision
  or builder identifier, so correlation among houses from the same development cannot be checked; we
  note this as a limitation.

These violations (right skew, heavy tail, and variance increasing with the mean) will be addressed in
Part 2, for example with a Box-Cox/log transformation of price; nothing is corrected here.
